pending_commit.commit_message: FROMGIT: rtw88: not to enter or leave PS under IRQ Remove PS related *_irqsafe functions to avoid entering/leaving PS under interrupt context. Instead, make PS decision in watch_dog. This could simplify the logic and make the code look clean. But it could have a little side-effect that if the driver is having heavy traffic before the every-2-second watch_dog detect the traffic and decide to leave PS, the thoughput will be lower. Once traffic is detected by watch_dog and left PS state, the throughput will resume to the peak the hardware ought to have again. Signed-off-by: Yan-Hsuan Chuang <yhchuang@realtek.com> Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org> (cherry picked from commit 61d7309562b51e9600f69ca70f9edf71f841fee7 git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/kvalo/wireless-drivers-next.git master) BUG=b:124400293 TEST=None Change-Id: Ic5bc1d329ecc1c1f12a47286ac3c3220a1c5182b Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1710449 Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: rtw88: not to control LPS by each vif The original design of LPS enter/leave routines allows to control the LPS state by each interface. But the hardware cannot actually handle it that way. This means the hardware can only enter LPS once with an associated port, so there is no need to keep tracking the state of each vif. Hence the logic of enter/leave LPS state can be simple, just to check the state of the device's flag. And for leaving LPS state, it will get the same port id to send to inform the hardware. Signed-off-by: Yan-Hsuan Chuang <yhchuang@realtek.com> Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org> (cherry picked from commit 3d391c06d917a18f846aa2a0ab155cb6c92ca6ea git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/kvalo/wireless-drivers-next.git master) BUG=b:124400293 TEST=None Change-Id: I7f0ba54609973557dd423cb3a823766215922802 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1710450 Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: rtw88: leave PS state for dynamic mechanism Dynamic mechanism requires BB/RF working to adjust hardware settings. But PS state periodically turns off BB/RF, could lead to wrong setting. So leave PS state before DM to make sure it works. And then check if we can enter PS state again. Signed-off-by: Yan-Hsuan Chuang <yhchuang@realtek.com> Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org> (cherry picked from commit 37ba5de2e731afbfe606d7192a8aeba625abdaba git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/kvalo/wireless-drivers-next.git master) BUG=b:124400293 TEST=Keep connected, and move around, if not leave LPS, dynamic mechanism could be broken, and disconnected (low opportunity) Change-Id: I173dac42d48320bc0e522a4fb2e3db7e7ec2eb30 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1710453 Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: rtw88: add deep power save support Deep power save allows firmware/hardware to operate in a lower power state. And the deep power save mode depends on LPS mode. So, before entering deep PS, driver must first enter LPS mode. Under Deep PS, most of hardware functions are shutdown, driver will not be able to read/write registers and transfer data to the device. Hence TX path must be protected by each interface. Take PCI for example, DMA engine should be idle, and no nore activities on the PCI bus. If driver wants to operate on the device, such as register read/write, it must first acquire the mutex lock and wake up from Deep PS, otherwise the behavior is undefined. Signed-off-by: Yan-Hsuan Chuang <yhchuang@realtek.com> Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org> (cherry picked from commit 27e117e4b01b5e699a40a3891b4f6924f99011d7 git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/kvalo/wireless-drivers-next.git master) BUG=b:124400293 TEST=None Change-Id: Ia15d98d9440ad8aa47804a182d4134aff2a90829 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1710454 Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: rtw88: select deep PS mode when module is inserted Add a module parameter to select deep PS mode. And the mode cannot be changed after the module has been inserted and probed. If anyone wants to change the deep mode, should change the mode and probe the device again to setup the changed deep mode. When the device is probed, driver will check the deep PS mode with different IC's PS mode suppotability. If none of the PS mode is matched, the deep PS mode is changed to NONE, means deep PS is disabled. Signed-off-by: Yan-Hsuan Chuang <yhchuang@realtek.com> Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org> (cherry picked from commit d3be4d115be05b1b4323286bc69de9e577fc9a0f git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/kvalo/wireless-drivers-next.git master) BUG=b:124400293 TEST=None Change-Id: I1f5a0393c96ec2d244cec72b90bc3df509a02d64 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1710456 Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: rtw88: add deep PS PG mode for 8822c Compare with LCLK mode, PG mode saves more power, by turning off more circuits. Therefore, to recover from PG mode, driver needs to backup some information into rsvd page. Such as CAM entries, DPK results. As CAM entries can change, it is required to re-download CAM entries after set_key. Signed-off-by: Yan-Hsuan Chuang <yhchuang@realtek.com> Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org> (cherry picked from commit 04b786e00987c5495dd9a374deb9c9d7f650a9da git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/kvalo/wireless-drivers-next.git master) BUG=b:124400293 TEST=None Change-Id: Ib1f34a349c92c66434601255ec6d77fcba21f249 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1710458 Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: rtw88: remove misleading module parameter rtw_fw_support_lps The module parameter rtw_fw_support_lps is misleading. It is not used to represent the firmware's property, but to determine if driver wants to ask firmware to enter LPS. However, driver should better enable/disable PS through cfg80211_ops::set_power_mgmt instead. For example, one could use iw command to set PS state. $ sudo iw wlanX set power_save [on/off] So rtw_fw_support_lps should be removed because it is misleading and useless. Instead of checking the parameter, set PS mode according to IEEE80211_CONF_PS. Signed-off-by: Yan-Hsuan Chuang <yhchuang@realtek.com> Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org> (cherry picked from commit bcde60e599fb044744b4e379ab74ea323a75ce5e git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/kvalo/wireless-drivers-next.git master) BUG=b:124400293 BUG=b:139546321 TEST=set power_save by iw, and see if driver is still sending H2C 0x20 periodically to enter/leave LPS state Change-Id: Ia2bacade7ae082e11a7e0e3fde413aa09ae30362 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1775694 Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

More broadly match arm machine types by looking for "arm" or "aarch64" as the beginning of the string.
